author: Vieillot, 1817
summary: 2009년 6월 23–24일 인천 옹진군 소청도에서 한 마리가 관찰된 것이 국내 첫 기록인 길잃은새다. 인도와 스리랑카에서 동남아시아, 중국 남부에 걸쳐 대체로 한곳에 머물러 사는 새로, 야자나무가 자라는 트인 땅이나 숲 사이 빈터, 경작지에서 지낸다. 높은 나뭇가지나 전깃줄에 앉아 있다가 날아올라 공중에서 곤충을 잡으며, 여러 마리가 한 가지에 바짝 붙어 앉는 습성이 있다.

pale pinkish-buff underparts, paler than the grey throat

young: 어린새는 윗면에 담황갈색 가로무늬가 있고 날개덮깃 끝이 적갈색이며, 아랫면에도 가로무늬가 있다.

art.subject: Ashy Woodswallow (Artamus fuscus), adult: head and throat dark ash-grey, darkest around the lores and eye; mantle and back ash-grey, a little paler than the head; rump and uppertail coverts whitish, forming a pale band above the tail; wings dark grey; underparts pinkish-grey to buff-grey, paler on the belly and vent; tail short, dark grey, narrowly tipped white. Bill thick, conical, pale blue-grey with a dark tip; dark eye; legs dark grey.
art.pose: perched upright on an exposed dead branch, side view
art.scene: Dead treetop at the edge of farmland on a Korean offshore island in May, during spring migration, bright light; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view perched upright on a bare dead branch: stocky with a large head, dark grey head and throat with a darker mask between eye and bill, stout finch-like pale blue-grey bill, grey back, long pointed dark grey wings reaching to or beyond the tail tip, pale pinkish-buff underparts, whiter undertail coverts, short dark tail tipped white

adult, in flight seen squarely from above: broad-based, pointed triangular wings spread straight out to the sides to their full span, dark grey head, grey back, narrow pale rump band above the short, spread dark tail tipped white, head, body and tail in a straight line
art.build: Stocky, short-tailed bird, a little smaller than a Brown-eared Bulbul, with a big head and short neck. Bill thick-based, conical and slightly decurved, shorter than the head. Legs short. Long, broad-based, pointed wings that at rest reach or slightly extend beyond the tip of the short, square tail. In flight the wings look triangular, like a large swallow or a starling; it glides and circles after insects. Often perches huddled side by side with others on a bare branch.
avoid: Do not paint a forked tail or tail streamers; the tail is short and square.
Do not paint a thin swallow bill; the bill is thick, conical and blue-grey.
Do not paint white underparts; they are pinkish to buffy grey.
Do not omit the pale rump band.
